title: fix(app-shell,i18n): a submitter's own recall is not an override, and an override recall says what a recall does (objectui#13225)
body:
Fixes #13225

Clause-②: yes

## What was wrong

On a pending approval request, `DeclaredActionsBar` labelled the Recall button **Override Recall** for every viewer with admin-override rights, and gave it the decision sentence: "Continuing uses your admin override: it finalises the step immediately and bypasses the approvers who have not acted — NAMES. The decision is recorded as an admin override."

Two viewers got it:

- a submitter who is also an admin (`can_act: false`, `is_submitter: true`, `can_override: true`), who was told that recalling their own request is an override;
- an admin who holds no slot and did not submit the request, who was told the recall finalises the step and is recorded as an admin override.

## The producer, and what a recall does (measured at the pin, not assumed)

Read at objectui's pinned objectstack SHA (`.objectstack-sha`, `f4755a68a`):

- `approval_recall` in `sys-approval-request.object.ts` declares its `visible` gate as the submitter arm (status pending or returned, and `record.viewer.is_submitter == true`) OR the admin-override arm `record.viewer.can_override == true`. The second arm came in with objectstack#12716. `actionAdmittedByOverride` finds `can_override` in that text, so `isOverrideDecision` admitted the recall for any viewer with `can_act: false` and `can_override: true`, including the submitter.
- `attachViewers` serves `is_submitter` as a plain boolean owner check, and serves `can_override` as true only on a `pending` request.
- `ApprovalService.recall`: when the override admits the caller, it skips the submitter check. It writes one `sys_approval_action` row with `action: 'recall'` and no `via_override`; the decision and reassign writers set that column, recall does not. It sets the request to `status: 'recalled'` with `pending_approvers` cleared, empties the approver index, mirrors `recalled` into the record's approval-status field when one is configured, and resumes the owning run with `decision: 'recall'`. Nothing records an override.

Measured on the bar at BASE (`58798eca8`): the corrected fixture and the new pins were run before the fix. The submitter-admin's button carried `data-override-decision="true"` and read "Override Recall". The override-only admin's notice was the decision sentence quoted above, word for word, in both its named and unnamed forms.

## The change

- `utils/approvalOverride.ts`: `isOverrideDecision` now also asks whether the viewer holds the lever through its submitter arm. For a lever whose declared gate names `is_submitter`, the override is the only way in only when the served flag is exactly `false`. It reads the served flag and the action's own gate, never an action-name list. The fail-safe direction is unchanged: an absent or non-boolean flag reads as "not an override". A lever whose gate does not name `is_submitter` (approve, reject, reassign) is judged exactly as before. The stale header line ("`approval_recall` / `approval_resubmit` gate on `is_submitter` and never match") now describes the shipped declaration.
- `views/DeclaredActionsBar.tsx`: `approvalRouteVerb` now also reads the `/recall` route, and a recall override gets its own notice, in a named and an unnamed form. It keeps the override framing (the "Override Recall" label and the amber treatment), says what a recall does, and says nothing about finalising the step or an override record:
  - named: "You did not submit this request. Continuing uses your admin override: the request is withdrawn, the record is unlocked, and the approvers who have not acted can no longer act on it — {{who}}."
  - unnamed: "You did not submit this request. Continuing uses your admin override: the request is withdrawn, any approver who has not acted can no longer act on it, and the record is unlocked."
- All ten packs gain `approvalsInbox.overrideRecallNotice` and `approvalsInbox.overrideRecallNoticeWho` as real translations, each written in that pack's existing words for recall, submitter, unlock and admin override. No existing key or value changes.
- The approve, reject and reassign sentences are byte-for-byte unchanged. The request the bar sends is unchanged too: same target, method and params, and a recall carries no decision outputs.
- One changeset, `.changeset/13225-override-recall-notice.md`: `@object-ui/app-shell` and `@object-ui/i18n`, both patch.

Clause-② turned out `yes`: two keys were added, which widens the exported `TranslationKeys`. Nothing narrows.

## Tests

Final readings at `c32944a0b`: commit `1cf5d98b6`, plus a merge of `main` at `f0300beff`, which brings in the landed objectui#13227. Each exit code was captured on its own, before any pipe.

- `DeclaredActionsBar.overrideAffordance.test.tsx`: the recall fixture now declares the shipped gate (the submitter arm OR `can_override`, reduced to the spelling this suite evaluates), plus the shipped description and params. A new describe block holds seven pins: the submitter-admin case, the plain-submitter control, the override-only admin case with names and without, the approve and reassign controls, approve still flagged as an override for a submitter-admin, and an unchanged request. The expected sentences are read from the `en` pack.
- `approvalOverride.test.ts`: the recall and resubmit gates are copied verbatim from the declaration. New pins cover recall admitted by the override arm, the submitter's own recall not counted as an override, an override-only admin's recall counted as one, a fail-safe answer when `is_submitter` is absent or not a boolean, and the approve control for a submitter-admin.
- Targeted, before the merge: 6 files (the four `DeclaredActionsBar` suites, `approvalOverride.test.ts` and `useConsoleActionRuntime.overrideNotice.test.tsx`) gave `Test Files 6 passed (6)`, `Tests 116 passed (116)`.
- Blast radius at `c32944a0b`: 68 test files found by `git grep` for `approvalOverride`, the three predicates, `overrideNotice`, `DeclaredActionsBar`, `approvalsInbox`, `approval_recall` and `product-neutral`, across app-shell, apps/console, components, core, react, plugin-detail, plugin-grid and scripts. Result: `Test Files 68 passed (68)`, `Tests 968 passed (968)`.
- i18n package at `c32944a0b`: `pnpm exec vitest run packages/i18n/` gave `Test Files 84 passed (84)`, `Tests 1319 passed | 13 skipped (1332)`.

**Ablation**, run after the fix commit at `1cf5d98b6`. Both source files were set back to their BASE blobs while the packs and tests stayed at HEAD. On-disk hashes matched BASE (`86de7b3e8` for the bar, `7b83f4400` for the helper), and `grep -c` dropped `mayHoldAsSubmitter` from 2 to 0 and `overrideRecallNotice` from 2 to 0. The run gave `Tests 6 failed | 50 passed (56)`, exactly the six recall pins. The Received values are the card's Actual: `data-override-decision` "true", button text "Override Recall", and the decision sentence in both forms. The restore was `git checkout HEAD --` under a trap. On-disk hashes then matched the HEAD blobs (`f27b4ab0e`, `37ac56dd8`) and `git diff HEAD` was 0 bytes. No dist step was needed: the suites reach the bar and the helper by relative import, and the pack through the vitest source alias. No ablation file was kept.

## Acceptance notes

- An admin who holds a slot on the request but did not submit it also reaches Recall only through the override arm (the recall's gate has no `can_act` arm), yet still sees the plain Recall. `isOverrideOnlyViewer` requires `can_act: false`, and this change keeps that precondition, so the only viewer relabelled is the one the card's Expected names: no slot, not the submitter. This is the module's tolerated fail-safe direction, and nothing in that dialog is false: the declared description still reads "Recall this request? Approvers can no longer act on it and the record is unlocked." Not filed.
- Two sibling fixtures still declare the recall submitter-only, the shape it had before objectstack#12716: `RecordDetailView.approvalDeclaredActions.test.tsx` (app-shell) and `approvalRequestsDataSource.decisionPage.test.tsx` (apps/console). Neither renders an override-capable viewer against the recall, so neither hides a defect today, and both are outside this claim's file surface. Not filed.
- The override recall dialog states the effect twice: the notice, then the declared description. The reject override already has the same shape. The notice has to stand on its own, because a translation bundle can replace the declared description.
- "The record is unlocked" is stated unconditionally, as the declared description and the card's Expected state it. On a node with `lockRecord: false`, the record was never locked to begin with.
